passage_text: Researchers at the University of Health Sciences conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the efficacy of a novel antihypertensive agent, Hypotensol, in reducing systolic blood pressure (SBP) among adults with stage 1 hypertension. One hundred and twenty participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) Hypotensol 10 mg daily, (2) Hypotensol 20 mg daily, or (3) placebo. Baseline SBP was measured after a 5‑minute seated rest using an automated cuff. After 4 weeks of treatment, SBP was re‑measured under identical conditions. The study aimed to determine whether the higher dose produced a greater reduction in SBP compared to the lower dose and placebo. Table 1 summarizes the mean SBP values and the mean change from baseline for each group.
stem: Which of the following best describes the change in systolic blood pressure for the 20 mg Hypotensol group?
explanation: The mean change is calculated as baseline minus week‑4 SBP: 147 mmHg − 123 mmHg = 24 mmHg decrease.
trap: Option D incorrectly interprets the change as an increase.

stem: Which experimental design best matches the study described?
explanation: Participants were randomly assigned to treatment groups and outcomes were measured prospectively, which is the hallmark of a randomized controlled trial.
trap: Option A describes a snapshot study and does not involve randomization.

stem: Calculate the average change in systolic blood pressure across all three groups.
explanation: Average change = (−13 + (−24) + (−6)) ÷ 3 = −14.33 mmHg, rounded to −14.3 mmHg.

stem: Which of the following statements is NOT supported by the passage and Table 1?

options.A: The 20 mg group had the greatest reduction in SBP.
options.B: The placebo group also experienced a reduction in SBP.
options.C: Hypotensol was shown to be safe for long-term use.
options.D: The baseline SBP values were similar across groups.

explanation: Correct: C) The trial lasted 4 weeks and reported only SBP, so long-term safety was not assessed. Why the others are wrong: A) the 20 mg group fell by 24 mmHg, more than 13 or 6. B) the placebo group fell by 6 mmHg (146 to 140). D) baseline values were 145, 147 and 146 mmHg.
trap: Assuming a short 4-week blood pressure trial also shows long-term safety, which it did not measure.

stem: The placebo group's SBP fell by 6 mmHg. Which explanation is most appropriate?

options.A: Placebo effect and regression to the mean

explanation: A change in the placebo arm cannot be a drug effect. It reflects the placebo effect, regression to the mean (participants were enrolled for high readings) and measurement variability, which is why a placebo control is needed.
trap: Attributing any change to the drug; the placebo arm shows what happens without active treatment.
